data.content_ref: inline:The target contains an internal contradiction. Its mechanism declares, 'It follows that the underlying structure was never relevant to the outcome at all,' yet the entire mechanism depends on structure being relevant: theories are selected 'for corroboration,' preference 'maximize[s] error elimination,' and 'the fittest (most tested) theories are the only ones available for further mutation and testing.' Testing, corroboration, and error elimination are all structural relations between a theory's content and the evidence it confronts. If structure were truly irrelevant to the outcome, there would be no reason the 'most tested' theories are fitter than untested ones — the selection process would be indifferent to whether a theory has any empirical content at all. The target thus simultaneously relies on the structural relationship between theory and evidence to drive selection and denies that this structure matters, collapsing its own explanation.
